Economic and Social Council 
 Session XLVI 
 Sponsors: Commonwealth of Australia, Federal Republic of Brazil, Dominion of Canada, 
 Germany, Japan, Federation of Malaysia, Republic of the Philippines, Sri Lanka, United 
 Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, United States of America 
 Signatories: Republic of Colombia, French Republic, Republic of Panama, Islamic Republic of 
 Pakistan, Kingdom of Norway, Ukraine 
 Helping the Global Economy Recover From the Invasion of Ukraine 
 The General Assembly, 
 Conscious of  the many problems food inflation is causing  in Ukraine and other member 
 nations severely impacted by the invasion, such as increased cost of living, lower purchasing 
 power, increased poverty, and increased unemployment, 
 Deeply concerned  by the widespread displacement of  individuals caused by the 
 unprovoked invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation, many of whom have extensive 
 knowledge of agriculture, infrastructure, and sustainable energy, 
 Considering  the benefits that integration of refugees  could offer, including the potential to 
 drive innovation in sustainable practices, stimulate economic growth, reduce the reliance of 
 refugees on humanitarian aid, and promote a greater degree of social cohesion and mutual 
 understanding between host communities and refugee populations, 
 Alarmed  by the recent inflation rate  of food prices at 20%, the increase in 
 unemployment, the decrease in job opportunities, and the general struggling economy of Ukraine 
 and other nations impacted by the unprovoked invasion, 
 1.  Demands  that the Russian Federation immediately withdraw  from Ukraine; 
 a.  The unprovoked attack on Ukraine has spiraled into a global crisis and a 
 vicious cycle of inflation, poverty, and unemployment has severely 
 hindered the global economy; 
 b.  The withdrawal of Russia from Ukraine would facilitate the reconstruction 
 of infrastructure in Ukraine and allow the global economy to recover; 
 i. 
 The Russian Federation would be forced to compensate for the 
 repair of 80% of damaged infrastructure, thereby expediting the 
 process of reconstruction; 
 2.  Requests  that all mentally and physically capable refugees will be offered 
 incentives to help with the construction and maintenance of the Allied 
 Agricultural Institution (refer to clause 5); 
 a.  These incentives shall include the support services offered in the fifth 
 clause along with a guaranteed base income that is 25% higher than that of 
 the country the refugee is working in; 
 3.  Calls upon  the creation of the Allied Agricultural  Institution (AAI), which will be 
 devoted to further combating the inflation of food prices, most notably corn, 
 grains, livestock, and other various fruits; 
 a.  The countries hosting these farms will include, but not limited to, Brazil, 
 Panama, Colombia, Turkey, the United States, the Philippines, and 
 Australia; 
 i. 
 Considering the suitability of the terrain of these countries and the 
 fact that they are geographically the furthest from the conflict, they 
 would make perfect candidates for potential agricultural hosts of 
 the AAI; 
 b.  The money generated from the AAI, in collaboration with the World Food 
 Programme (WFP), will help increase the GDP of host nations and foreign 
 investors of the AAI, which will, in turn, help make more funds available 
 to support the rebuilding of Ukraine’s infrastructure and lower food 
 inflation; 
 c.  The AAI is set to secure financial backing from prominent countries 
 including Brazil, Turkey, Australia, the United Kingdom, France, and the 
 United States along with the WFP, which is expected to be paid back from 
 the revenue generated from the AAI within ten years; 
 i. 
 The respective countries will each pay a minimum of 30 Million 
 USD to help fund the building of the farms; 
 ii. 
 80 million dollars shall be requested from the WFP; 
 iii. 
 The money shall be sent to the AAI and preamble planning shall be 
 completed by June 1st, 2024 to allow for food inflation to be 
 lowered promptly; 
 4.  Proposes  a 40 Million USD plan which will supply  aircraft currently being unused by 
 airlines to fly refugees from Ukraine to the designated AAI compounds; 
 a.  This funding will be raised by investments made by NATO and foreign investors 
 including the nations listed above in clause 3; 
 b.  Refugees will begin to be flown over on January 1st, 2024 after the preamble 
 planning is completed and the AAIs are ready to be constructed; 
 5.  Proclaims  that refugees from the Russian Federation’s unprovoked invasion of 
 Ukraine who are helping with the implementation of the AAI should be strategically 
 integrated into their host country’s economy; 
 a.  These refugees should be provided with adequate shelter, access to food and 
 healthcare, primary education, and legal services, along with vocational training 
 and training specific to the construction of the agricultural institutions; 
 i. 
 These support services will be provided by already existing United 
 Nations Organizations, such as the UNHCR, working in the nations where 
 the agricultural institutions will be constructed; 
 b.  These support services will cost around 90-100 million USD in total per 10,000 
 refugees; 
 c.  If all of these support services are adequately implemented, the initial investment 
 will be offset after economies recover from the Russian invasion; 
 i. 
 The refugees will be helping to build and run the agricultural institutions, 
 which will create new jobs and lower the 20% food inflation levels to a 
 more sustainable level, while also helping to increase the GDP of AAI 
 host countries, foreign investors, and Ukraine; 
 d.  The most vital of these support services including shelter and food shall be 
 provided upon the arrival of the refugees, with the remaining services being fully 
 deployed by January 1st, 2025; 
 7.  Calls upon the creation of  the Export Diversion  Program (EDP), which would divert 
 Ukrainian agricultural exports to the Mediterranean Sea via rail to bypass the Black Sea 
 blockade; 
 a.  The railroad route will extend from Athens to Uzhhorod by connecting 
 existing routes throughout Eastern Europe; 
 b.  Expenses for the construction of railroads would partially be supported by 
 the above nations while additional funds could be obtained from the 
 WTO; 
 8.  Calls upon  the creation of a task force that helps  Ukraine and other nations most 
 significantly impacted by the invasion of Ukraine; 
 a.  The Task Force Supporting Nations Impacted by the Russian Invasion will 
 help to rebuild infrastructure, provide job training, create new jobs, and 
 provide humanitarian aid to Ukraine; 
 b.  Additionally, this task force will create jobs in nations whose economies 
 have been significantly impacted by the invasion; 
 i. 
 This will be done by partnering with both the public and private 
 sectors by creating new investment opportunities for foreign 
 investors, investing in small businesses, and employing citizens to 
 help rebuild infrastructure which will automatically create jobs; 
 c.  It will also be a priority to lower the number of youth who are not in 
 education, employment, or training (NEET) in Ukraine and the other 
 nations impacted by the invasion; 
 i. 
 This will specifically be done by partnering with UNICEF to 
 provide labor education to teens and young adults while also 
 helping unemployed and educated youth enter the workforce; 
 d.  A budget determined on a country-by-country basis will be funded by 
 NATO, the nations and foreign investors mentioned above, and NGOs; 
 9.  Encourages  the creation of a Financial Fair Play  Plan ensuring that no scandalous acts 
 involving imports, exports, and independent monetary and fiscal policies occur; 
 a.  Countries that commit scandalous acts such as the invasion will be met with harsh 
 punishments deemed appropriate to the circumstance, some of which may include 
 sanctions; 
 10.  Encourages  the implementation of tighter monetary  policies to combat inflation; 
 a.  The stricter monetary policies will help to regulate a country’s money supply, 
 interest rates, and overall financial system and inflation levels; 
 i. 
 The stricter monetary policies will be effective as soon as possible; 
 b.  The global economy would greatly benefit from stronger monetary policies as 
 they would promote price stability, manage exchange rates, stimulate economic 
 growth, and manage financial stability; 
 c.  These monetary policies will be overlooked by the World Bank; 
 i. 
 Independent monetary policies will still exist and be strengthened, as 
 dependency on a single monetary policy would slow global economic 
 growth and increase inflation; 
 d.  Free trade agreements will also be provided by NATO for countries that invest in 
 this resolution.
